newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Bunds firm but shy away from key resistance.
newsitem.headline: German Bunds firm but shy away from key resistance.

text.p: German debt prices drifted higher in afternoon trade, aided by gains in some of Europe's periheral bond markets.
But traders said that with tough technical resistance at 101.58 remaining in place, the market's upmove was not particularly convincing.
By 1432 GMT, the September DTB Bund future was seven basis points up on the day at 101.39, having blipped to a high at 101.56 earlier in the session.
In the cash market, the 10-year benchmark Bund was quoted at 102.02 for a 5.721 percent bid yield.

"The easing in Treasury prices has capped the gains in the German market," said one trader in Frankfurt. He added that futures the market was likely to remain in the now well-tracked range of around 101.10 to 101.58 in the next few sessions.

Analysts said consumer price data from three of the four German states were in line with market forecasts, and suggested that the preliminary data for the whole of west Germany were likely to show a 0.2 percent month-on-month gain and 1.6 year-on-year gain in June.
"The CPI data were bang in line," said Charles Diebel, senior fixed income analyst at Technical data in London.
On the technical basis, Diebel too said that 101.58 was the key hurdle for the September Bund contract.

"If we got up through 101.58 then things would begin to look pretty constructive and we could get back to the highs of 101.88 and as far as 102.00," he said. "But I can't really see the justification for that kind of rally at the moment."
Diebel said that with the EMU situation remaining much the same, there was little reason for Bunds to make any significant move in either direction.
On spreads, Bunds outpaced the U.S. market, pushing the yield spread out to 82 basis points from 75 previously.
